Why Live in Merida?
-------------------

Enjoy luxury living in one of the most beautiful colonial cities in Mexico. Known as the “cultural capital” of the Mexico Yucatan Peninsula, Merida is a vibrant, welcoming city 

Merida is known as _ciudad blanca_ (white city) because of the heavy use of white limestone as a building material, although as you roam the grid-like streets you can expect to find homes and shops decorated in delightful pastel colors.

Stroll down colorful streets, sip coffee in charming cafes, and spend your free time exploring the magnificent monuments and historic buildings. You’ll never run out of things to do in Merida! 

The Top 10 Best Things to Do in Merida
--------------------------------------

### 1\. Discover Local Yucatan Cuisine

Merida is home to some of the best food in Mexico, and while favorites like tacos and _elote_ (corn) Merida boasts some delicious regional dishes that are a must-try for any foodie.

With roots in Mayan cooking but heavily influenced by Europe, the Caribbean, and other regions throughout Mexico, Yucatan cuisine is unique, delicious, and distinctive from anywhere else in Mexico.

Some of our favorite dishes are:

*   **Huevos Motuleños:** a Yucatan specialty breakfast dish of fried eggs over black beans on a fried tortilla, served with salsa, plantains, chorizo, and queso fresco.
*   **Queso relleno:** a hollowed-out ball of Edam cheese filled with ground pork and smothered in gravy.
*   **Poc-chuc:** a traditional Mayan dish marinated of thinly-sliced pork marinated in sour orange juice and served with pickled onions.
*   **Cochinita pibil (Yucatán-style barbecued pork):** this dish of pulled pork shoulder marinated and braised in achiote paste, orange juice, and lime is perfect for tacos.

### 2\. Stroll the Boutiques at Casa Tho

Casa Tho Concept House is named after the Mayan name for Merida, T’hō, and is the perfect place to stroll around on a lazy afternoon.

This stunning renovated mansion offers a handful of boutique shops selling jewelry, clothing, perfumes, and more.

### 3\. Get Lost in the Lucas de Galvez Market Merida

Merida’s main market, the Lucas de Galvez market is a bustling market that dates back to the late 1800s when it was just a small shed.

Nowadays, the market is a sprawling, chaotic, and a great place to pick up fruits, vegetables, handmade local crafts, and lots more. 

### 4\. Celebrate at One of Merida’s Annual Festivals

Merida boasts a variety of annual festivals and events, including:

*   Merida Fest (January)
*   Carnival of Merida (February)
*   Semana Santa Processions (April)
*   La Noche Blanca (May)
*   Mexican Independence Day (September)
*   Day of the Dead (November)
*   Christmas (December)

These are just a handful of events and festivals you can enjoy living in Merida!

### 5\. Grab a Bite at Merida’s Restaurant Row

Located at the southern end of Paseo Montejo to Calle 47 (47th Street) you can find “restaurant row”, a stretch of places to eat and drink that will satisfy any appetite.

Some of our favorite restaurants include:

*   [Cafe Latte Quattro Sette](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d12103961-Reviews-Latte_Quattro_Sette-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-MYF7YpUpFBMQ6ZsIpNYqV)
    : A gorgeous coffee shop with decadent pastries.
*   [Catrin](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d13483140-Reviews-El_Catrin-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-OMpZ6rAQPopqNb2mPm3oA)
    : A hip gastropub with funky artwork on the walls
*   [Oliva Enoteca](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d7720030-Reviews-Oliva_Enoteca-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-ZmZxeFM7el7UPIPFemPAb)
    : An upscale Italian restaurant with a great wine list
*   [Amado by The Beer Box](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g150811-d23193817-Reviews-Amado_By_The_Beer_Box-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html)
    : A beautiful indoor/outdoor restaurant with live jazz several nights a week

### 6\. Go Organic at the Slow Food Market

Looking for a  more upscale farmer’s market experience? Then spend a Saturday strolling through the Slow Food Market.

It’s the perfect place to pick up organic meat, produce, as well as oils, fresh-baked goods, and other artisanal products.

### 7\. Join the BiciRuta

On Sunday mornings, both residents and tourists alike come out for a city-wide bike ride from 8 AM – 12 PM!

BiciRuta means “bike route’ is one of the most popular things to do in Merida, offering free bike and paid bike rentals as well as a chance to people-watch as you cruise around the city.

### 8\. Catch a Game of Pok Ta Pok

Pok Ta Pok is an ancient sport that is re-enacted every week in front of the Cathedral. Every Wednesday, head down to watch players fight it out to the sounds of traditional music.

The players slide along the cobblestones while attempting to score by hitting the ball into the post using just their hips. 

There’s no Pok Ta Pok league (the game is re-created for entertainment purposes) but that doesn’t mean that it isn’t a fun and exciting spectacle that you can catch every week while living in Merida.

### 9\. Grab a Drink (or Two, or Three)

Happy hour runs late in Merida, and there’s no shortage of places to grab cervezas, margaritas, micheladas, or palomas. You can even try pox (pronounced poche) which is a regional specialty drink made from corn.

If traditional cantinas aren’t your thing, there’s a growing craft beer scene with new options popping up in the centro all the time.

### 10\. Dance in the Streets During a Weekly Fiesta

There’s something to do every night in Merida! At night the city’s streets and plazas light up and come to life with dances, performances, concerts, and more. 

On weekends, several of the main streets are closed to traffic and street performers spill out into the streets. 

Featuring regional music and dance, these events are open to the public and are often lined with food trucks and pop-up stalls in case you feel hungry after dancing the night away.

### Living in Merida Mexico

Now that you’ve learned about all there is to see and do in Merida, it’s time to find your dream property! [Contact us today](https://www.meridarealestategroup.com/contact-us/)
 to enjoy luxury, upscale living in Merida, Mexico.

Why Live in Merida?
-------------------

Enjoy luxury living in one of the most beautiful colonial cities in Mexico. Known as the “cultural capital” of the Mexico Yucatan Peninsula, Merida is a vibrant, welcoming city 

Merida is known as _ciudad blanca_ (white city) because of the heavy use of white limestone as a building material, although as you roam the grid-like streets you can expect to find homes and shops decorated in delightful pastel colors.

Stroll down colorful streets, sip coffee in charming cafes, and spend your free time exploring the magnificent monuments and historic buildings. You’ll never run out of things to do in Merida! 

The Top 10 Best Things to Do in Merida
--------------------------------------

### 1\. Discover Local Yucatan Cuisine

Merida is home to some of the best food in Mexico, and while favorites like tacos and _elote_ (corn) Merida boasts some delicious regional dishes that are a must-try for any foodie.

With roots in Mayan cooking but heavily influenced by Europe, the Caribbean, and other regions throughout Mexico, Yucatan cuisine is unique, delicious, and distinctive from anywhere else in Mexico.

Some of our favorite dishes are:

*   **Huevos Motuleños:** a Yucatan specialty breakfast dish of fried eggs over black beans on a fried tortilla, served with salsa, plantains, chorizo, and queso fresco.
*   **Queso relleno:** a hollowed-out ball of Edam cheese filled with ground pork and smothered in gravy.
*   **Poc-chuc:** a traditional Mayan dish marinated of thinly-sliced pork marinated in sour orange juice and served with pickled onions.
*   **Cochinita pibil (Yucatán-style barbecued pork):** this dish of pulled pork shoulder marinated and braised in achiote paste, orange juice, and lime is perfect for tacos.

### 2\. Stroll the Boutiques at Casa Tho

Casa Tho Concept House is named after the Mayan name for Merida, T’hō, and is the perfect place to stroll around on a lazy afternoon.

This stunning renovated mansion offers a handful of boutique shops selling jewelry, clothing, perfumes, and more.

### 3\. Get Lost in the Lucas de Galvez Market Merida

Merida’s main market, the Lucas de Galvez market is a bustling market that dates back to the late 1800s when it was just a small shed.

Nowadays, the market is a sprawling, chaotic, and a great place to pick up fruits, vegetables, handmade local crafts, and lots more. 

### 4\. Celebrate at One of Merida’s Annual Festivals

Merida boasts a variety of annual festivals and events, including:

*   Merida Fest (January)
*   Carnival of Merida (February)
*   Semana Santa Processions (April)
*   La Noche Blanca (May)
*   Mexican Independence Day (September)
*   Day of the Dead (November)
*   Christmas (December)

These are just a handful of events and festivals you can enjoy living in Merida!

### 5\. Grab a Bite at Merida’s Restaurant Row

Located at the southern end of Paseo Montejo to Calle 47 (47th Street) you can find “restaurant row”, a stretch of places to eat and drink that will satisfy any appetite.

Some of our favorite restaurants include:

*   [Cafe Latte Quattro Sette](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d12103961-Reviews-Latte_Quattro_Sette-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-MYF7YpUpFBMQ6ZsIpNYqV)
    : A gorgeous coffee shop with decadent pastries.
*   [Catrin](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d13483140-Reviews-El_Catrin-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-OMpZ6rAQPopqNb2mPm3oA)
    : A hip gastropub with funky artwork on the walls
*   [Oliva Enoteca](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d7720030-Reviews-Oliva_Enoteca-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-ZmZxeFM7el7UPIPFemPAb)
    : An upscale Italian restaurant with a great wine list
*   [Amado by The Beer Box](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g150811-d23193817-Reviews-Amado_By_The_Beer_Box-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html)
    : A beautiful indoor/outdoor restaurant with live jazz several nights a week

### 6\. Go Organic at the Slow Food Market

Looking for a  more upscale farmer’s market experience? Then spend a Saturday strolling through the Slow Food Market.

It’s the perfect place to pick up organic meat, produce, as well as oils, fresh-baked goods, and other artisanal products.

### 7\. Join the BiciRuta

On Sunday mornings, both residents and tourists alike come out for a city-wide bike ride from 8 AM – 12 PM!

BiciRuta means “bike route’ is one of the most popular things to do in Merida, offering free bike and paid bike rentals as well as a chance to people-watch as you cruise around the city.

### 8\. Catch a Game of Pok Ta Pok

Pok Ta Pok is an ancient sport that is re-enacted every week in front of the Cathedral. Every Wednesday, head down to watch players fight it out to the sounds of traditional music.

The players slide along the cobblestones while attempting to score by hitting the ball into the post using just their hips. 

There’s no Pok Ta Pok league (the game is re-created for entertainment purposes) but that doesn’t mean that it isn’t a fun and exciting spectacle that you can catch every week while living in Merida.

### 9\. Grab a Drink (or Two, or Three)

Happy hour runs late in Merida, and there’s no shortage of places to grab cervezas, margaritas, micheladas, or palomas. You can even try pox (pronounced poche) which is a regional specialty drink made from corn.

If traditional cantinas aren’t your thing, there’s a growing craft beer scene with new options popping up in the centro all the time.

### 10\. Dance in the Streets During a Weekly Fiesta

There’s something to do every night in Merida! At night the city’s streets and plazas light up and come to life with dances, performances, concerts, and more. 

On weekends, several of the main streets are closed to traffic and street performers spill out into the streets. 

Featuring regional music and dance, these events are open to the public and are often lined with food trucks and pop-up stalls in case you feel hungry after dancing the night away.

### Living in Merida Mexico

Now that you’ve learned about all there is to see and do in Merida, it’s time to find your dream property! [Contact us today](https://www.meridarealestategroup.com/contact-us/)
 to enjoy luxury, upscale living in Merida, Mexico.

Why Live in Merida?
-------------------

Enjoy luxury living in one of the most beautiful colonial cities in Mexico. Known as the “cultural capital” of the Mexico Yucatan Peninsula, Merida is a vibrant, welcoming city 

Merida is known as _ciudad blanca_ (white city) because of the heavy use of white limestone as a building material, although as you roam the grid-like streets you can expect to find homes and shops decorated in delightful pastel colors.

Stroll down colorful streets, sip coffee in charming cafes, and spend your free time exploring the magnificent monuments and historic buildings. You’ll never run out of things to do in Merida! 

The Top 10 Best Things to Do in Merida
--------------------------------------

### 1\. Discover Local Yucatan Cuisine

Merida is home to some of the best food in Mexico, and while favorites like tacos and _elote_ (corn) Merida boasts some delicious regional dishes that are a must-try for any foodie.

With roots in Mayan cooking but heavily influenced by Europe, the Caribbean, and other regions throughout Mexico, Yucatan cuisine is unique, delicious, and distinctive from anywhere else in Mexico.

Some of our favorite dishes are:

*   **Huevos Motuleños:** a Yucatan specialty breakfast dish of fried eggs over black beans on a fried tortilla, served with salsa, plantains, chorizo, and queso fresco.
*   **Queso relleno:** a hollowed-out ball of Edam cheese filled with ground pork and smothered in gravy.
*   **Poc-chuc:** a traditional Mayan dish marinated of thinly-sliced pork marinated in sour orange juice and served with pickled onions.
*   **Cochinita pibil (Yucatán-style barbecued pork):** this dish of pulled pork shoulder marinated and braised in achiote paste, orange juice, and lime is perfect for tacos.

### 2\. Stroll the Boutiques at Casa Tho

Casa Tho Concept House is named after the Mayan name for Merida, T’hō, and is the perfect place to stroll around on a lazy afternoon.

This stunning renovated mansion offers a handful of boutique shops selling jewelry, clothing, perfumes, and more.

### 3\. Get Lost in the Lucas de Galvez Market Merida

Merida’s main market, the Lucas de Galvez market is a bustling market that dates back to the late 1800s when it was just a small shed.

Nowadays, the market is a sprawling, chaotic, and a great place to pick up fruits, vegetables, handmade local crafts, and lots more. 

### 4\. Celebrate at One of Merida’s Annual Festivals

Merida boasts a variety of annual festivals and events, including:

*   Merida Fest (January)
*   Carnival of Merida (February)
*   Semana Santa Processions (April)
*   La Noche Blanca (May)
*   Mexican Independence Day (September)
*   Day of the Dead (November)
*   Christmas (December)

These are just a handful of events and festivals you can enjoy living in Merida!

### 5\. Grab a Bite at Merida’s Restaurant Row

Located at the southern end of Paseo Montejo to Calle 47 (47th Street) you can find “restaurant row”, a stretch of places to eat and drink that will satisfy any appetite.

Some of our favorite restaurants include:

*   [Cafe Latte Quattro Sette](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d12103961-Reviews-Latte_Quattro_Sette-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-MYF7YpUpFBMQ6ZsIpNYqV)
    : A gorgeous coffee shop with decadent pastries.
*   [Catrin](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d13483140-Reviews-El_Catrin-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-OMpZ6rAQPopqNb2mPm3oA)
    : A hip gastropub with funky artwork on the walls
*   [Oliva Enoteca](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d7720030-Reviews-Oliva_Enoteca-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-ZmZxeFM7el7UPIPFemPAb)
    : An upscale Italian restaurant with a great wine list
*   [Amado by The Beer Box](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g150811-d23193817-Reviews-Amado_By_The_Beer_Box-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html)
    : A beautiful indoor/outdoor restaurant with live jazz several nights a week

### 6\. Go Organic at the Slow Food Market

Looking for a  more upscale farmer’s market experience? Then spend a Saturday strolling through the Slow Food Market.

It’s the perfect place to pick up organic meat, produce, as well as oils, fresh-baked goods, and other artisanal products.

### 7\. Join the BiciRuta

On Sunday mornings, both residents and tourists alike come out for a city-wide bike ride from 8 AM – 12 PM!

BiciRuta means “bike route’ is one of the most popular things to do in Merida, offering free bike and paid bike rentals as well as a chance to people-watch as you cruise around the city.

### 8\. Catch a Game of Pok Ta Pok

Pok Ta Pok is an ancient sport that is re-enacted every week in front of the Cathedral. Every Wednesday, head down to watch players fight it out to the sounds of traditional music.

The players slide along the cobblestones while attempting to score by hitting the ball into the post using just their hips. 

There’s no Pok Ta Pok league (the game is re-created for entertainment purposes) but that doesn’t mean that it isn’t a fun and exciting spectacle that you can catch every week while living in Merida.

### 9\. Grab a Drink (or Two, or Three)

Happy hour runs late in Merida, and there’s no shortage of places to grab cervezas, margaritas, micheladas, or palomas. You can even try pox (pronounced poche) which is a regional specialty drink made from corn.

If traditional cantinas aren’t your thing, there’s a growing craft beer scene with new options popping up in the centro all the time.

### 10\. Dance in the Streets During a Weekly Fiesta

There’s something to do every night in Merida! At night the city’s streets and plazas light up and come to life with dances, performances, concerts, and more. 

On weekends, several of the main streets are closed to traffic and street performers spill out into the streets. 

Featuring regional music and dance, these events are open to the public and are often lined with food trucks and pop-up stalls in case you feel hungry after dancing the night away.

### Living in Merida Mexico

Now that you’ve learned about all there is to see and do in Merida, it’s time to find your dream property! [Contact us today](https://www.meridarealestategroup.com/contact-us/)
 to enjoy luxury, upscale living in Merida, Mexico.

Why Live in Merida?
-------------------

Enjoy luxury living in one of the most beautiful colonial cities in Mexico. Known as the “cultural capital” of the Mexico Yucatan Peninsula, Merida is a vibrant, welcoming city 

Merida is known as _ciudad blanca_ (white city) because of the heavy use of white limestone as a building material, although as you roam the grid-like streets you can expect to find homes and shops decorated in delightful pastel colors.

Stroll down colorful streets, sip coffee in charming cafes, and spend your free time exploring the magnificent monuments and historic buildings. You’ll never run out of things to do in Merida! 

The Top 10 Best Things to Do in Merida
--------------------------------------

### 1\. Discover Local Yucatan Cuisine

Merida is home to some of the best food in Mexico, and while favorites like tacos and _elote_ (corn) Merida boasts some delicious regional dishes that are a must-try for any foodie.

With roots in Mayan cooking but heavily influenced by Europe, the Caribbean, and other regions throughout Mexico, Yucatan cuisine is unique, delicious, and distinctive from anywhere else in Mexico.

Some of our favorite dishes are:

*   **Huevos Motuleños:** a Yucatan specialty breakfast dish of fried eggs over black beans on a fried tortilla, served with salsa, plantains, chorizo, and queso fresco.
*   **Queso relleno:** a hollowed-out ball of Edam cheese filled with ground pork and smothered in gravy.
*   **Poc-chuc:** a traditional Mayan dish marinated of thinly-sliced pork marinated in sour orange juice and served with pickled onions.
*   **Cochinita pibil (Yucatán-style barbecued pork):** this dish of pulled pork shoulder marinated and braised in achiote paste, orange juice, and lime is perfect for tacos.

### 2\. Stroll the Boutiques at Casa Tho

Casa Tho Concept House is named after the Mayan name for Merida, T’hō, and is the perfect place to stroll around on a lazy afternoon.

This stunning renovated mansion offers a handful of boutique shops selling jewelry, clothing, perfumes, and more.

### 3\. Get Lost in the Lucas de Galvez Market Merida

Merida’s main market, the Lucas de Galvez market is a bustling market that dates back to the late 1800s when it was just a small shed.

Nowadays, the market is a sprawling, chaotic, and a great place to pick up fruits, vegetables, handmade local crafts, and lots more. 

### 4\. Celebrate at One of Merida’s Annual Festivals

Merida boasts a variety of annual festivals and events, including:

*   Merida Fest (January)
*   Carnival of Merida (February)
*   Semana Santa Processions (April)
*   La Noche Blanca (May)
*   Mexican Independence Day (September)
*   Day of the Dead (November)
*   Christmas (December)

These are just a handful of events and festivals you can enjoy living in Merida!

### 5\. Grab a Bite at Merida’s Restaurant Row

Located at the southern end of Paseo Montejo to Calle 47 (47th Street) you can find “restaurant row”, a stretch of places to eat and drink that will satisfy any appetite.

Some of our favorite restaurants include:

*   [Cafe Latte Quattro Sette](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d12103961-Reviews-Latte_Quattro_Sette-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-MYF7YpUpFBMQ6ZsIpNYqV)
    : A gorgeous coffee shop with decadent pastries.
*   [Catrin](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d13483140-Reviews-El_Catrin-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-OMpZ6rAQPopqNb2mPm3oA)
    : A hip gastropub with funky artwork on the walls
*   [Oliva Enoteca](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d7720030-Reviews-Oliva_Enoteca-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-ZmZxeFM7el7UPIPFemPAb)
    : An upscale Italian restaurant with a great wine list
*   [Amado by The Beer Box](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g150811-d23193817-Reviews-Amado_By_The_Beer_Box-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html)
    : A beautiful indoor/outdoor restaurant with live jazz several nights a week

### 6\. Go Organic at the Slow Food Market

Looking for a  more upscale farmer’s market experience? Then spend a Saturday strolling through the Slow Food Market.

It’s the perfect place to pick up organic meat, produce, as well as oils, fresh-baked goods, and other artisanal products.

### 7\. Join the BiciRuta

On Sunday mornings, both residents and tourists alike come out for a city-wide bike ride from 8 AM – 12 PM!

BiciRuta means “bike route’ is one of the most popular things to do in Merida, offering free bike and paid bike rentals as well as a chance to people-watch as you cruise around the city.

### 8\. Catch a Game of Pok Ta Pok

Pok Ta Pok is an ancient sport that is re-enacted every week in front of the Cathedral. Every Wednesday, head down to watch players fight it out to the sounds of traditional music.

The players slide along the cobblestones while attempting to score by hitting the ball into the post using just their hips. 

There’s no Pok Ta Pok league (the game is re-created for entertainment purposes) but that doesn’t mean that it isn’t a fun and exciting spectacle that you can catch every week while living in Merida.

### 9\. Grab a Drink (or Two, or Three)

Happy hour runs late in Merida, and there’s no shortage of places to grab cervezas, margaritas, micheladas, or palomas. You can even try pox (pronounced poche) which is a regional specialty drink made from corn.

If traditional cantinas aren’t your thing, there’s a growing craft beer scene with new options popping up in the centro all the time.

### 10\. Dance in the Streets During a Weekly Fiesta

There’s something to do every night in Merida! At night the city’s streets and plazas light up and come to life with dances, performances, concerts, and more. 

On weekends, several of the main streets are closed to traffic and street performers spill out into the streets. 

Featuring regional music and dance, these events are open to the public and are often lined with food trucks and pop-up stalls in case you feel hungry after dancing the night away.

### Living in Merida Mexico

Now that you’ve learned about all there is to see and do in Merida, it’s time to find your dream property! [Contact us today](https://www.meridarealestategroup.com/contact-us/)
 to enjoy luxury, upscale living in Merida, Mexico.

#### Property Description

El Pueblo Mérida is a boutique hotel set at the beginning of Paseo de Montejo, placing it in one of the city’s most recognizable cultural corridors while maintaining a calm, inward-facing atmosphere. The property offers 9 suites and 13 bathrooms, built across a 1,904 m² lot (20,494 sq ft) with approximately 1,639 m² of construction (17,642 sq ft).

This is a hospitality property defined by breathing room. In a market where many central Mérida hotels prioritize density, El Pueblo Mérida is arranged around open courtyards, gardens, and shared spaces with comfortable proportions. The result is an experience that feels unhurried, with natural light moving through the property and a layout that supports privacy as much as connection.

At the heart of the design is a 25 m naturally treated pool (82 ft), free of chemical additives and long enough to feel like a true wellness feature rather than a decorative amenity. Its placement anchors the grounds and shapes the daily rhythm of the property, from early swims to quiet afternoons in the garden.

Operational features are thoughtfully integrated. Soundproofed suites support rest and discretion, while an elevator improves accessibility across floors. A dedicated gym serves longer-stay guests and wellness-minded travelers. The chef’s kitchen is built for consistent service and flexible programming, and the onsite café adds a welcoming point of arrival that can extend the guest experience beyond the rooms.

The location offers a strong relationship with the city. Paseo de Montejo provides immediate access to Mérida’s restaurants, galleries, museums, and architectural landmarks, while the property’s internal plan preserves a sense of retreat. For an owner, this balance supports a boutique concept with year-round appeal in a destination known for safety, culture, and a growing international audience.

El Pueblo Mérida is well-suited to continued boutique hotel operation, a repositioning under a branded concept, or a more curated hospitality approach focused on design, wellness, and experience. Above all, it is a Mérida asset with tangible differentiators: land and build scale in a central setting, a signature natural pool, and amenities that support both guest satisfaction and smooth day-to-day management.

In a market where many central Mérida hotels prioritize density, El Pueblo Mérida is arranged around open courtyards, gardens, and shared spaces with comfortable proportions. The result is an experience that feels unhurried, with natural light moving through the property and a layout that supports privacy as much as connection.



At the heart of the design is a 25 m naturally treated pool (82 ft), free of chemical additives and long enough to feel like a true wellness feature rather than a decorative amenity. Its placement anchors the grounds and shapes the daily rhythm of the property, from early swims to quiet afternoons in the garden.



Operational features are thoughtfully integrated. Soundproofed suites support rest and discretion, while an elevator improves accessibility across floors. A dedicated gym serves longer-stay guests and wellness-minded travelers. The chef’s kitchen is built for consistent service and flexible programming, and the onsite café adds a welcoming point of arrival that can extend the guest experience beyond the rooms.



The location offers a strong relationship with the city. Paseo de Montejo provides immediate access to Mérida’s restaurants, galleries, museums, and architectural landmarks, while the property’s internal plan preserves a sense of retreat. For an owner, this balance supports a boutique concept with year-round appeal in a destination known for safety, culture, and a growing international audience.



El Pueblo Mérida is well-suited to continued boutique hotel operation, a repositioning under a branded concept, or a more curated hospitality approach focused on design, wellness, and experience. Above all, it is a Mérida asset with tangible differentiators: land and build scale in a central setting, a signature natural pool, and amenities that support both guest satisfaction and smooth day-to-day management.

#### Property Description

This expansive three-bedroom residence at LUSSELA Montecristo is designed for refined urban living, offering exceptional scale, privacy, and a level of comfort rarely found in boutique residential developments. Located within one of Mérida’s most established and prestigious residential neighborhoods, the residence forms part of an intimate collection of just eleven homes, where discretion and long-term livability are central to the experience.

The residence spans approximately 309 square meters (3,327 square feet) and is organized to balance generous interior volumes with seamless indoor-outdoor living. The layout is anchored by an open-plan living and dining area that flows naturally toward a private terrace, creating a central space suited for both everyday life and elegant entertaining. Large openings allow natural light to define the interiors while maintaining a calm, composed atmosphere throughout the home.

The primary suite is thoughtfully positioned to provide privacy and comfort, featuring a walk-in closet and a spacious en-suite bathroom finished with clean lines and understated materials. Two additional bedrooms, each with their own bathroom and ample storage, are proportioned to function independently, making the residence equally well suited for family living or hosting guests for extended stays. A dedicated service room with bathroom, linen storage, and a laundry area are discreetly integrated into the plan, reinforcing the home’s suitability for full-time residence.

Interior finishes reflect a restrained approach to luxury, prioritizing durability, proportion, and timeless appeal. High-quality materials, carefully selected lighting, and a functional open kitchen contribute to an environment that feels both elevated and livable. The residence includes two assigned parking spaces and private storage, completing a layout designed for convenience without compromise.

As a resident of LUSSELA, owners enjoy access to a concierge-led lifestyle supported by a curated selection of shared spaces. These include a formal lobby with concierge service, business center, club room, game room, fitness and wellness center, and rooftop amenities featuring an infinity pool, terrace, and whisky and cigar lounge. The development’s low-density design and residential focus create an atmosphere that is private, composed, and distinctly non-transient.

This three-bedroom residence represents a rare opportunity to enjoy generous space, architectural clarity, and personalized service within one of Mérida’s most desirable residential settings, offering a level of comfort and discretion aligned with international luxury standards.

This expansive three-bedroom residence at LUSSELA Montecristo is designed for refined urban living, offering exceptional scale, privacy, and a level of comfort rarely found in boutique residential developments. The residence spans approximately **309 square meters (3,327 square feet)** and is organized to balance generous interior volumes with seamless indoor-outdoor living. The layout is anchored by an open-plan living and dining area that flows naturally toward a private terrace, creating a central space suited for both everyday life and elegant entertaining. Large openings allow natural light to define the interiors while maintaining a calm, composed atmosphere throughout the home.

The primary suite is thoughtfully positioned to provide privacy and comfort, featuring a walk-in closet and a spacious en-suite bathroom finished with clean lines and understated materials. Two additional bedrooms, each with their own bathroom and ample storage, are proportioned to function independently, making the residence equally well suited for family living or hosting guests for extended stays. A dedicated service room with bathroom, linen storage, and a laundry area are discreetly integrated into the plan, reinforcing the home’s suitability for full-time residence.

Interior finishes reflect a restrained approach to luxury, prioritizing durability, proportion, and timeless appeal. High-quality materials, carefully selected lighting, and a functional open kitchen contribute to an environment that feels both elevated and livable. The residence includes **two assigned parking spaces** and private storage, completing a layout designed for convenience without compromise.

As a resident of LUSSELA, owners enjoy access to a concierge-led lifestyle supported by a curated selection of shared spaces. These include a formal lobby with concierge service, business center, club room, game room, fitness and wellness center, and rooftop amenities featuring an infinity pool, terrace, and whisky and cigar lounge. The development’s low-density design and residential focus create an atmosphere that is private, composed, and distinctly non-transient.

This three-bedroom residence represents a rare opportunity to enjoy generous space, architectural clarity, and personalized service within one of Mérida’s most desirable residential settings, offering a level of comfort and discretion aligned with international luxury standards.

#### Property Description

The 3-bedroom residences at DUNAS are designed for those seeking generous space, flexibility, and a refined beachfront lifestyle in one of Yucatán’s most desirable coastal settings. These residences are well suited for families, extended stays, or owners who value comfort without compromise.

Each residence features **three spacious bedrooms**, including a primary suite with a private bathroom and thoughtful separation from the secondary bedrooms. A versatile **flex space** adds adaptability, ideal for use as a home office, media room, or additional guest area. In total, the layout includes **four full bathrooms**, ensuring privacy and ease for both residents and visitors.

The living and dining areas are arranged in an open yet well-defined layout, anchored by a modern kitchen designed for daily use and entertaining. Expansive sliding doors lead to a **private terrace**, extending the living space outdoors and allowing for natural light, cross-ventilation, and seamless indoor-outdoor flow. Select residences include **private pools**, creating an enhanced outdoor living experience.

The residence design prioritizes comfort, circulation, and flexibility, with proportions that accommodate full-time living or extended coastal stays.

Residents enjoy full access to DUNAS’ beachfront amenity collection, including a swimming pool, padel court, social gym, children’s playground, palapas, grill area, snack bar, landscaped common areas, storage units, and controlled access. The result is a well-balanced residence that combines space, design, and lifestyle in a true beachfront environment.

og:description: Discover Dunas Beachfront 3 Bedroom Condo, a 1788 ft², 3 Bed Condo located in Beachfront Chuburna, priced at $531195 USD. HOA/Maintenance: $0 USD/Month

The 3-bedroom residences at DUNAS are designed for those seeking generous space, flexibility, and a refined beachfront lifestyle in one of Yucatán’s most desirable coastal settings. These residences are well suited for families, extended stays, or owners who value comfort without compromise.



Each residence features three spacious bedrooms, including a primary suite with a private bathroom and thoughtful separation from the secondary bedrooms. A versatile flex space adds adaptability, ideal for use as a home office, media room, or additional guest area. In total, the layout includes four full bathrooms, ensuring privacy and ease for both residents and visitors.



The living and dining areas are arranged in an open yet well-defined layout, anchored by a modern kitchen designed for daily use and entertaining. Expansive sliding doors lead to a private terrace, extending the living space outdoors and allowing for natural light, cross-ventilation, and seamless indoor-outdoor flow. Select residences include private pools, creating an enhanced outdoor living experience.



The residence design prioritizes comfort, circulation, and flexibility, with proportions that accommodate full-time living or extended coastal stays.



Residents enjoy full access to DUNAS’ beachfront amenity collection, including a swimming pool, padel court, social gym, children’s playground, palapas, grill area, snack bar, landscaped common areas, storage units, and controlled access. The result is a well-balanced residence that combines space, design, and lifestyle in a true beachfront environment.

#### Property Description

The 2-bedroom residences at DUNAS are thoughtfully designed to offer a comfortable and functional beachfront lifestyle, ideal for full-time living, vacation use, or investment in one of Yucatán’s most desirable coastal destinations.

Each residence features two well-proportioned bedrooms, including a primary suite with a private bathroom, complemented by a versatile flex space that can be used as a home office, guest area, or additional living space. The layout includes three full bathrooms, providing convenience and privacy for both residents and guests.

The interior design emphasizes open, light-filled living areas, with a seamless connection between the living room, dining area, and kitchen. Large sliding doors open to a private terrace, creating an easy flow between indoor and outdoor spaces and allowing residents to enjoy natural ventilation and the coastal atmosphere. Select ground-floor residences include private pools, enhancing the outdoor living experience.

Carefully planned proportions and efficient circulation make the residence feel spacious and adaptable, while the flex space adds valuable versatility for different lifestyles and uses.

Owners enjoy full access to DUNAS’ beachfront amenities, including a swimming pool, padel court, social gym, children’s playground, palapas, grill area, snack bar, landscaped common areas, storage units, and controlled access. Together, these elements create a relaxed yet well-appointed residential environment designed for enjoying life by the sea.

#### Property Description

The 4-bedroom residences at MADEIRA are designed for spacious coastal living, offering generous layouts, privacy, and a seamless balance between indoor and outdoor spaces. Ideal for full-time living or refined second-home use, these residences combine functionality with thoughtful design throughout.

Each residence features **four well-proportioned bedrooms**, including a primary suite with a private balcony, en-suite bathroom, and ample closet space. Two additional secondary bedrooms each include their own en-suite bathrooms, while a dedicated service bedroom with a full bathroom adds flexibility for staff, guests, or extended family use. In total, the layout includes **four full bathrooms and one half bathroom**, ensuring comfort and convenience across all living areas.

The social areas are open and inviting, with a defined living room, dining area, and a modern kitchen designed for both everyday use and entertaining. A spacious **private terrace off the main living area** extends the interior outward, creating an ideal setting for relaxed gatherings and coastal breezes.

Additional features include a **family room**, laundry area, and assigned storage, enhancing day-to-day practicality. The residence’s design emphasizes natural light, cross-ventilation, and a fluid connection between spaces.

Located within the MADEIRA residential tower in Chicxulub, owners enjoy access to a full suite of amenities including a swimming pool, fitness center, indoor and outdoor social areas, children’s play space, controlled access, and on-site security. The result is a well-balanced residence offering comfort, scale, and a complete lifestyle in one of Yucatán’s most appealing coastal settings.

#### Property Description

Set within the private and highly regarded Bosques de Altabrisa residential community, this distinguished single-level home offers an exceptional combination of space, privacy, and refined functionality in one of Mérida’s most established neighborhoods.

Designed for effortless living and entertaining, the residence spans approximately 913.77 m² (9,836 sq ft) of construction on a 891.05 m² (9,590 sq ft) lot, all thoughtfully arranged on one level for seamless flow and accessibility.

The interior layout balances openness and separation with intention. Formal living and dining areas are positioned independently from the kitchen, creating distinct yet connected spaces for daily living and gatherings. The fully equipped kitchen serves as a central hub, featuring a generous island for casual dining and premium appliances, including a Sub-Zero refrigerator and Wolf range, blending performance with understated elegance.

The home features four spacious bedrooms, each with a private en-suite bathroom and walk-in closet, offering comfort and privacy for family and guests alike. In total, the residence includes seven full bathrooms and one half bath, ensuring convenience across all living areas.

Outdoor living is equally considered. A covered terrace opens to a private swimming pool and landscaped garden, creating a tranquil setting for relaxation and social occasions. Covered parking for three vehicles, a service room, and a dedicated laundry area further enhance day-to-day practicality.

Located within a secure, gated community with 24-hour security, residents also enjoy access to shared amenities including landscaped green areas, children’s play spaces, multiple lounge areas, and a private event salon. The home’s position in Altabrisa places it moments from premier shopping centers, hospitals, universities, and key city arteries, offering both exclusivity and connectivity.

Delivery is immediate, presenting a rare opportunity to acquire a substantial, move-in-ready residence in one of Mérida’s most sought-after residential enclaves.

#### Property Description

60 Norte is a next-generation mixed-use destination where residences, business, gastronomy, hospitality, retail, and health come together around a grand central park. Designed as the new heart of the city’s north, it reimagines urban living with a vibrant, connected ecosystem that elevates daily life and long-term value.

#### Prime location & effortless connectivity

Set where **Calle 60**, Prolongación Paseo de Montejo, and the Periférico Norte converge, 60 Norte puts you minutes from top shopping, dining, culture, universities, hospitals, and corporate hubs. It offers direct routes to Centro Histórico, a straight shot to Progreso’s beaches, and quick access to the airport and Tren Maya links—so weekend escapes and global connections are always within reach.

#### A complete lifestyle around a central park

At the core of 60 Norte is a large, landscaped park—the social heart of the community—framed by destination dining, a hospitality center, and curated retail. The experience is designed for everyday wellness: morning coffee on the plaza, lunch meetings by the green, evening events under the lights, and quiet walks steps from home.

#### Residences for every stage of life

The residential component features **three elegant towers** with layouts tailored to families, couples, students, and professionals—prioritizing comfort, community, and a refined urban aesthetic. Living here means having daily essentials, workplaces, healthcare, and leisure all in one thoughtfully planned address.

#### Business & medical hubs built in

Codex Hub delivers modern office space that catalyzes motivation, efficiency, and innovation, while Codex Medical offers purpose-designed clinics and consultorios that enhance care and practice operations. Together, they anchor a professional ecosystem that supports premium living and long-term demand.

#### Architecture with a Mérida pedigree

Guided by the urban vision of Arq. Augusto Quijano Axle and developed by DESIGNIA, 60 Norte is crafted to transcend time, transforming an underused site into a multifaceted district that modernizes the city while honoring its character.

Why buyers and investors choose 60 Norte
----------------------------------------

*   Location advantage: Northern Mérida’s most connected crossroads with marquee neighbors—from The Harbor Lifestyle Mall to Museo del Mundo Maya.
*   Built-in demand drivers: On-site offices, medical, hospitality, and retail support strong rental prospects and long-term absorption.
*   Enduring value: A flagship development in a prestige corridor where appreciation is supported by infrastructure, services, and lifestyle appeal.

#### Property Description

For those who desire the ultimate in comfort, privacy, and modern design, Casa Mitos presents its exclusive 3-bedroom condos. These residences are designed to accommodate families, host guests, or provide ample room for a sophisticated lifestyle in the heart of Mérida.

#### Expansive Layouts for Modern Families

The 3-bedroom units (Type E) measure 135.5 m² (≈1,459 sq. ft.), making them the most spacious residences at Casa Mitos. Each home is designed with functionality and style in mind:

*   Three full bedrooms with built-in closets
*   Two and a half bathrooms with premium finishes
*   Spacious open living and dining areas
*   Full kitchen with modern appliances and elegant design
*   Laundry area and walk-in closet for convenience
*   Private balconies with park or city views

#### Exclusive Amenities for Everyday Comfort

Living in a 3-bedroom condo at Casa Mitos means enjoying a private home enhanced by resort-style amenities, including:

*   Rooftop pool and Sky Lounge with panoramic views
*   Fitness center, yoga, sauna, and wellness spaces
*   Paddle tennis court and landscaped green areas
*   Social hub, coworking stations, and event lounge
*   Concierge service, biometric access, and 24/7 security

#### A Prime Location in Via Montejo

Casa Mitos is part of Via Montejo, Mérida’s award-winning master development, just steps from The Harbor Lifestyle Mall, fine dining, hotels, and the financial district. With easy access to Mérida’s historic downtown, Progreso Beach, and the airport, residents enjoy the perfect balance between urban convenience and natural beauty.

#### Exceptional Value in Mérida’s Premium Market

the 3-bedroom condos represent one of the most attractive investment opportunities in Mérida. Offering abundant living space, upscale design, and access to world-class amenities, these units are ideal as a primary residence, vacation property, or long-term investment.

#### Property Description

Casa Mitos offers a refined collection of 2-bedroom condos crafted for those who desire more space, versatility, and elegance. With expansive interiors and a modern architectural design, these residences are ideal for families, professionals, or investors seeking a property in Mérida’s most dynamic development.

#### Spacious Floor Plans with Modern Finishes

The 2-bedroom floor plans range from 89 m² (≈959 sq. ft.) to 115 m² (≈1,237 sq. ft.), providing ample space for both everyday living and entertaining. Each unit includes:

*   Two full bedrooms with built-in closets and natural light
*   Open living and dining areas with direct balcony access
*   Modern kitchen with high-end finishes
*   Laundry area and smart storage solutions
*   Options with additional flex space for home office or guest use

#### Panoramic Views and Natural Light

Designed to maximize comfort and scenery, the C1 and C2 units feature large windows and private terraces with views of the Harbor Lifestyle Mall, the lake, the park, or city skyline. The D model, the largest 2-bedroom option, expands living space with generous layouts and premium views.

#### Exclusive Amenities for Everyday Luxury

Residents of Casa Mitos enjoy resort-style amenities, including:

*   Rooftop pool and Sky Lounge
*   Gym, yoga, and wellness areas
*   Paddle tennis court and pet park
*   Social and coworking hubs
*   Concierge services, biometric access, and CCTV security

#### Prime Location in Via Montejo

Set within Via Montejo, Mérida’s premier mixed-use development, Casa Mitos connects you directly to The Harbor Lifestyle Mall, financial district, dining, entertainment, and international institutions. Mérida’s historic downtown, Progreso Beach, and the airport are just minutes away, blending urban convenience with natural escapes.

#### Attractive Price Points

Casa Mitos’ 2-bedroom condos offer an exceptional opportunity to own a luxury property in one of Mexico’s safest and fastest-growing cities. Perfect as a primary residence, vacation retreat, or high-yield rental investment, these condos deliver both lifestyle and long-term value.

*   Rooftop pool & Sky Lounge

#### Property Description

Casas Caracol is a thoughtfully designed residential project located in the heart of Mérida Centro. Just a few blocks from Parque Santa Ana and Paseo Montejo, these homes offer a comfortable, practical, and well-built living option in one of the city’s most walkable and culturally rich neighborhoods. Whether you’re looking for a full-time home, a vacation property, or a long-term investment in a growing market, Casas Caracol offers convenience, style, and functionality in a central location.

#### Comfortable Layouts with Regional Character

Each home features 170 m² (1,829 ft²) of total construction on a 140 m² (1,506 ft²) lot, with 143 m² (1,540 ft²) of enclosed living space. The layout includes two bedrooms, each with its own full bathroom, closet space, and a desk area—ideal for remote work or study. There’s also a guest bathroom, a fully equipped kitchen, laundry area, and an open living-dining space that connects directly to a private terrace with a pool. On the rooftop, a garden area provides additional outdoor space for relaxing or entertaining.

#### Built with Local Materials and Practical Finishes

Casas Caracol homes are built with long-lasting materials and inspired by Yucatecan architecture. Features include chukum finishes, traditional Yucatán-style doors, cedar wood carpentry, terrazzo floors, and bajareque-style accents. High ceilings and natural ventilation keep the homes comfortable, while thoughtful details like dimmable lights and ambient lighting add warmth to the space.

#### Smart Infrastructure and Energy Efficiency

The homes are equipped with practical systems designed for everyday use and long-term savings. Each house includes preparation for solar panels, a 1,200-liter buried water cistern, 750-liter water tank with pump, and a water softener with active carbon and sediment filters. Additional features include an electric boiler, photovoltaic sensor lighting, a swimming pool system with pump and filter, and air conditioning installed in all rooms.

#### Functional Features for Everyday Living

Designed with daily comfort in mind, Casas Caracol homes also include modern touches like TV and internet outlets in all rooms and rooftop, electrically operated upper windows, garbage disposal and mailbox prep, and secure lighting and water systems. These details make the homes easy to maintain, live in, or manage as rental properties.

#### Prime Location in the Historic Center of Mérida

The location is one of Casas Caracol’s strongest assets. You’ll be just 3 blocks from Parque Santa Ana, 4 blocks from Paseo Montejo, and a short walk from Mérida Cathedral and La Plancha Park. Local restaurants, cafes, galleries, and shops are all nearby, making it easy to enjoy the best of Mérida without needing a car.

#### Optional Furniture Package Available

For buyers who want a ready-to-use home, a furniture package is available. This makes the property a great choice for those looking to move in quickly or begin using it as a vacation rental right away.

#### FAQ

**What makes the location of Casas Caracol special?**

Casas Caracol is located in Mérida Centro, just 3 blocks from Parque Santa Ana and 4 blocks from the famous Paseo Montejo. This area is one of the most desirable and walkable parts of the city, with easy access to restaurants, cafes, markets, galleries, museums, and parks like La Plancha, which features walking trails, a food hall, and cultural spaces.

**Is the neighborhood safe and suitable for full-time living?**

Yes. Mérida Centro is one of the safest and most livable urban neighborhoods in Mexico. Many residents are full-time locals and international homeowners who value the historic charm, walkability, and vibrant culture. The homes are designed with secure systems, including outdoor lighting and mailboxes, and garbage access through secure exterior doors.

**What are some nearby attractions and amenities?**

In addition to Parque Santa Ana, the homes are a short walk to the gastronomic corridor of Calle 47, the La Plancha urban park, local art galleries, artisan markets, and the city’s historic landmarks. You’ll also find pharmacies, supermarkets, yoga studios, and co-working spaces all within a few minutes’ walk.

#### Property Description

Located in the private community of Compostela in Santa María Yaxché, this well-designed two-story home offers comfort, space, and smart features in one of the most desirable areas of Mérida’s north. Set on a 565 m² (6,081 ft²) lot, with 406 m² (4,370 ft²) of interior space, the home is ideal for families looking for a move-in-ready property with quality finishes and access to excellent community amenities.

#### Comfortable Layout with Smart Upgrades

The home features a thoughtful layout and smart technology that adds convenience and peace of mind. It’s equipped with a Ring smart doorbell, Yale smart lock, video surveillance, 30 solar panels, and remote-controlled lighting and air conditioning.

Ground Floor:  
Spacious living and dining area with double-height ceilings. Fully equipped kitchen with Smeg appliances, granite counters, a wine fridge, and water purification system. There’s also a pantry and breakfast bar, guest half bath, and a bedroom with a full bathroom and walk-in closet—great for guests or multi-generational living. The ground floor includes a laundry room with washer/dryer, a service room with its own bath, and a covered terrace with a marble bar and sink. Outside you’ll find a chukum-finished pool, sun deck, garden with lighting and irrigation system, outdoor half bath, and storage space. The garage accommodates 2 covered vehicles and up to 5 uncovered.

#### Upper Floor: Privacy and Functionality

Upstairs, there are three additional bedrooms, each with air conditioning, blackout curtains, and its own full bathroom. The primary suite includes a walk-in closet, double vanity, indoor and outdoor showers, and a soaking tub. A cozy reading nook, built-in desk, and family TV room complete the upper level.

#### Community Amenities and Lifestyle

Compostela is a low-density private community with just 74 lots across 10 hectares, offering a peaceful environment and full access to: 24/7 gated security and trash collection, clubhouse with event spaces, spa with steam and sauna, business center, co-working space, cigar and snack bar, gym, swimming pools, play areas, and sports courts for tennis, paddle, and soccer.

#### Excellent Location in Northern Mérida

Casa Compostela is just minutes from top schools, hospitals, shopping, and restaurants, with easy access to main roads. It’s a great option for families or anyone looking for a well-built home in a quiet, secure, and well-located neighborhood. With smart features, energy efficiency, and great shared amenities, this home is a solid investment and a comfortable place to call home.

#### FAQ

**Is the home move-in ready?**

Yes. The home is being sold fully equipped, with appliances, smart systems, air conditioners, and built-in features already installed. It’s ready for immediate occupancy.

**What smart home features are included?**

Casa Compostela #61 comes with a Ring smart doorbell, Yale digital lock, remote-controlled lights and air conditioning, video surveillance cameras, and 30 rooftop solar panels for energy efficiency.

**What community amenities are available in Compostela?**

Compostela includes a clubhouse, swimming pools, gym, spa with sauna and steam room, co-working areas, children’s play zones, sports courts (tennis, paddle, soccer), and 24/7 gated security.

****Is the location convenient for schools, shopping, or healthcare?****

Yes. Casa Compostela is located in **northern Mérida**, close to top-rated schools, hospitals, shopping centers, and major roads, offering easy access to everything a family needs.

#### Property Description

Located in Mérida’s historic center, just a few blocks from Paseo Montejo and Parque La Mejorada, Casa Axiotic is a charming and well-preserved colonial home that offers the comfort of a modern renovation while staying true to its original character. This fully furnished property is ideal for those looking for a move-in-ready home in one of the most walkable and vibrant neighborhoods in the city.

#### Historic Design with Comfortable Living Spaces

Casa Axiotic has been carefully restored to maintain its colonial feel, featuring high ceilings, stone walls, natural finishes, and unique decorative touches throughout. The living room is furnished with vintage pieces, including a fully working gramophone and artwork made from natural axiote, which gives the home its name. The dining room has space for up to 12 people and is air-conditioned for comfort during the warmer months.

The kitchen is fully equipped with premium finishes, a center island, bar seating, and all the essentials for cooking and entertaining. There’s also a cozy TV room with stone wall accents, antique décor, and comfortable seating—offering a relaxed space for watching movies or reading.

#### Three Bedrooms with Bathrooms and Private Outdoor Areas

This home has three bedrooms, each with a full bathroom and walk-in closet. The main bedroom includes a four-poster bed, a private bath, and a small loft-style reading space. One guest bedroom is on the ground floor with easy access, while the third bedroom is upstairs with a balcony and space for a hammock—perfect for visitors or short-term rentals.

At the center of the home is a private garden and pool area, designed as a peaceful escape with lounge chairs, plants, and natural stone finishes. It’s a quiet and refreshing spot to enjoy Mérida’s climate without leaving home.

#### Rooftop Terrace with City Views

The home also features a rooftop terrace with views of Mérida’s historic rooftops. It includes a small grill area, sun loungers, and a shaded table with umbrella—great for casual get-togethers or enjoying the evening breeze.

#### Fully Furnished and Move-In Ready

Casa Axiotic is being sold fully furnished and decorated, just as shown in the listing photos and videos. It includes antique and custom pieces, air conditioning, and everything needed to move in or rent out immediately. The property is free of liens and ready for closing.

#### Great Location in Mérida’s Centro Histórico

Located just a short walk from Paseo Montejo, Parque La Mejorada, and the gastronomic corridor of Calle 47, this home is perfectly positioned for enjoying the best of Mérida. You’ll be close to restaurants, art galleries, shops, museums, and parks. The area is friendly and easy to explore on foot, making it ideal for daily life or hosting guests.

Casa Axiotic is a unique opportunity to own a home full of character and warmth, right in the center of one of Mexico’s most welcoming and culturally rich cities.

#### FAQ

**Is the home being sold furnished?**

Yes. The property is sold fully furnished and decorated, just as shown in the listing photos and video. This includes all major furniture, antique pieces, art, décor, and air conditioning, making it completely move-in ready or ideal for immediate rental use.

**What kind of outdoor spaces does the property offer?**

The home includes a private interior garden with a natural-stone swimming pool, lounge chairs, and tropical vegetation. There is also a rooftop terrace with city views, a grill area, a sun deck, and space for outdoor dining or relaxing.

**Where exactly is the home located in Mérida?**

Casa Axiotic is located in Mérida Centro, just a few blocks from Paseo Montejo, Parque La Mejorada, and the newly developed La Plancha park. It’s also close to the Gastronomic Corridor on Calle 47, offering easy access to top restaurants, cafes, and shops.

Why Live in Merida?
-------------------

Enjoy luxury living in one of the most beautiful colonial cities in Mexico. Known as the “cultural capital” of the Mexico Yucatan Peninsula, Merida is a vibrant, welcoming city 

Merida is known as _ciudad blanca_ (white city) because of the heavy use of white limestone as a building material, although as you roam the grid-like streets you can expect to find homes and shops decorated in delightful pastel colors.

Stroll down colorful streets, sip coffee in charming cafes, and spend your free time exploring the magnificent monuments and historic buildings. You’ll never run out of things to do in Merida! 

The Top 10 Best Things to Do in Merida
--------------------------------------

### 1\. Discover Local Yucatan Cuisine

Merida is home to some of the best food in Mexico, and while favorites like tacos and _elote_ (corn) Merida boasts some delicious regional dishes that are a must-try for any foodie.

With roots in Mayan cooking but heavily influenced by Europe, the Caribbean, and other regions throughout Mexico, Yucatan cuisine is unique, delicious, and distinctive from anywhere else in Mexico.

Some of our favorite dishes are:

*   **Huevos Motuleños:** a Yucatan specialty breakfast dish of fried eggs over black beans on a fried tortilla, served with salsa, plantains, chorizo, and queso fresco.
*   **Queso relleno:** a hollowed-out ball of Edam cheese filled with ground pork and smothered in gravy.
*   **Poc-chuc:** a traditional Mayan dish marinated of thinly-sliced pork marinated in sour orange juice and served with pickled onions.
*   **Cochinita pibil (Yucatán-style barbecued pork):** this dish of pulled pork shoulder marinated and braised in achiote paste, orange juice, and lime is perfect for tacos.

### 2\. Stroll the Boutiques at Casa Tho

Casa Tho Concept House is named after the Mayan name for Merida, T’hō, and is the perfect place to stroll around on a lazy afternoon.

This stunning renovated mansion offers a handful of boutique shops selling jewelry, clothing, perfumes, and more.

### 3\. Get Lost in the Lucas de Galvez Market Merida

Merida’s main market, the Lucas de Galvez market is a bustling market that dates back to the late 1800s when it was just a small shed.

Nowadays, the market is a sprawling, chaotic, and a great place to pick up fruits, vegetables, handmade local crafts, and lots more. 

### 4\. Celebrate at One of Merida’s Annual Festivals

Merida boasts a variety of annual festivals and events, including:

*   Merida Fest (January)
*   Carnival of Merida (February)
*   Semana Santa Processions (April)
*   La Noche Blanca (May)
*   Mexican Independence Day (September)
*   Day of the Dead (November)
*   Christmas (December)

These are just a handful of events and festivals you can enjoy living in Merida!

### 5\. Grab a Bite at Merida’s Restaurant Row

Located at the southern end of Paseo Montejo to Calle 47 (47th Street) you can find “restaurant row”, a stretch of places to eat and drink that will satisfy any appetite.

Some of our favorite restaurants include:

*   [Cafe Latte Quattro Sette](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d12103961-Reviews-Latte_Quattro_Sette-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-MYF7YpUpFBMQ6ZsIpNYqV)
    : A gorgeous coffee shop with decadent pastries.
*   [Catrin](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d13483140-Reviews-El_Catrin-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-OMpZ6rAQPopqNb2mPm3oA)
    : A hip gastropub with funky artwork on the walls
*   [Oliva Enoteca](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d7720030-Reviews-Oliva_Enoteca-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-ZmZxeFM7el7UPIPFemPAb)
    : An upscale Italian restaurant with a great wine list
*   [Amado by The Beer Box](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g150811-d23193817-Reviews-Amado_By_The_Beer_Box-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html)
    : A beautiful indoor/outdoor restaurant with live jazz several nights a week

### 6\. Go Organic at the Slow Food Market

Looking for a  more upscale farmer’s market experience? Then spend a Saturday strolling through the Slow Food Market.

It’s the perfect place to pick up organic meat, produce, as well as oils, fresh-baked goods, and other artisanal products.

### 7\. Join the BiciRuta

On Sunday mornings, both residents and tourists alike come out for a city-wide bike ride from 8 AM – 12 PM!

BiciRuta means “bike route’ is one of the most popular things to do in Merida, offering free bike and paid bike rentals as well as a chance to people-watch as you cruise around the city.

### 8\. Catch a Game of Pok Ta Pok

Pok Ta Pok is an ancient sport that is re-enacted every week in front of the Cathedral. Every Wednesday, head down to watch players fight it out to the sounds of traditional music.

The players slide along the cobblestones while attempting to score by hitting the ball into the post using just their hips. 

There’s no Pok Ta Pok league (the game is re-created for entertainment purposes) but that doesn’t mean that it isn’t a fun and exciting spectacle that you can catch every week while living in Merida.

### 9\. Grab a Drink (or Two, or Three)

Happy hour runs late in Merida, and there’s no shortage of places to grab cervezas, margaritas, micheladas, or palomas. You can even try pox (pronounced poche) which is a regional specialty drink made from corn.

If traditional cantinas aren’t your thing, there’s a growing craft beer scene with new options popping up in the centro all the time.

### 10\. Dance in the Streets During a Weekly Fiesta

There’s something to do every night in Merida! At night the city’s streets and plazas light up and come to life with dances, performances, concerts, and more. 

On weekends, several of the main streets are closed to traffic and street performers spill out into the streets. 

Featuring regional music and dance, these events are open to the public and are often lined with food trucks and pop-up stalls in case you feel hungry after dancing the night away.

### Living in Merida Mexico

Now that you’ve learned about all there is to see and do in Merida, it’s time to find your dream property! [Contact us today](https://www.meridarealestategroup.com/contact-us/)
 to enjoy luxury, upscale living in Merida, Mexico.

Why Live in Merida?
-------------------

Enjoy luxury living in one of the most beautiful colonial cities in Mexico. Known as the “cultural capital” of the Mexico Yucatan Peninsula, Merida is a vibrant, welcoming city 

Merida is known as _ciudad blanca_ (white city) because of the heavy use of white limestone as a building material, although as you roam the grid-like streets you can expect to find homes and shops decorated in delightful pastel colors.

Stroll down colorful streets, sip coffee in charming cafes, and spend your free time exploring the magnificent monuments and historic buildings. You’ll never run out of things to do in Merida! 

The Top 10 Best Things to Do in Merida
--------------------------------------

### 1\. Discover Local Yucatan Cuisine

Merida is home to some of the best food in Mexico, and while favorites like tacos and _elote_ (corn) Merida boasts some delicious regional dishes that are a must-try for any foodie.

With roots in Mayan cooking but heavily influenced by Europe, the Caribbean, and other regions throughout Mexico, Yucatan cuisine is unique, delicious, and distinctive from anywhere else in Mexico.

Some of our favorite dishes are:

*   **Huevos Motuleños:** a Yucatan specialty breakfast dish of fried eggs over black beans on a fried tortilla, served with salsa, plantains, chorizo, and queso fresco.
*   **Queso relleno:** a hollowed-out ball of Edam cheese filled with ground pork and smothered in gravy.
*   **Poc-chuc:** a traditional Mayan dish marinated of thinly-sliced pork marinated in sour orange juice and served with pickled onions.
*   **Cochinita pibil (Yucatán-style barbecued pork):** this dish of pulled pork shoulder marinated and braised in achiote paste, orange juice, and lime is perfect for tacos.

### 2\. Stroll the Boutiques at Casa Tho

Casa Tho Concept House is named after the Mayan name for Merida, T’hō, and is the perfect place to stroll around on a lazy afternoon.

This stunning renovated mansion offers a handful of boutique shops selling jewelry, clothing, perfumes, and more.

### 3\. Get Lost in the Lucas de Galvez Market Merida

Merida’s main market, the Lucas de Galvez market is a bustling market that dates back to the late 1800s when it was just a small shed.

Nowadays, the market is a sprawling, chaotic, and a great place to pick up fruits, vegetables, handmade local crafts, and lots more. 

### 4\. Celebrate at One of Merida’s Annual Festivals

Merida boasts a variety of annual festivals and events, including:

*   Merida Fest (January)
*   Carnival of Merida (February)
*   Semana Santa Processions (April)
*   La Noche Blanca (May)
*   Mexican Independence Day (September)
*   Day of the Dead (November)
*   Christmas (December)

These are just a handful of events and festivals you can enjoy living in Merida!

### 5\. Grab a Bite at Merida’s Restaurant Row

Located at the southern end of Paseo Montejo to Calle 47 (47th Street) you can find “restaurant row”, a stretch of places to eat and drink that will satisfy any appetite.

Some of our favorite restaurants include:

*   [Cafe Latte Quattro Sette](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d12103961-Reviews-Latte_Quattro_Sette-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-MYF7YpUpFBMQ6ZsIpNYqV)
    : A gorgeous coffee shop with decadent pastries.
*   [Catrin](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d13483140-Reviews-El_Catrin-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-OMpZ6rAQPopqNb2mPm3oA)
    : A hip gastropub with funky artwork on the walls
*   [Oliva Enoteca](https://go.skimresources.com/?id=172087X1664748&xs=1&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.tripadvisor.com%2FRestaurant_Review-g150811-d7720030-Reviews-Oliva_Enoteca-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html&xcust=things-to-do-in-merida-mexico_amcid-ZmZxeFM7el7UPIPFemPAb)
    : An upscale Italian restaurant with a great wine list
*   [Amado by The Beer Box](https://www.tripadvisor.com/Restaurant_Review-g150811-d23193817-Reviews-Amado_By_The_Beer_Box-Merida_Yucatan_Peninsula.html)
    : A beautiful indoor/outdoor restaurant with live jazz several nights a week

### 6\. Go Organic at the Slow Food Market

Looking for a  more upscale farmer’s market experience? Then spend a Saturday strolling through the Slow Food Market.

It’s the perfect place to pick up organic meat, produce, as well as oils, fresh-baked goods, and other artisanal products.

### 7\. Join the BiciRuta

On Sunday mornings, both residents and tourists alike come out for a city-wide bike ride from 8 AM – 12 PM!

BiciRuta means “bike route’ is one of the most popular things to do in Merida, offering free bike and paid bike rentals as well as a chance to people-watch as you cruise around the city.

### 8\. Catch a Game of Pok Ta Pok

Pok Ta Pok is an ancient sport that is re-enacted every week in front of the Cathedral. Every Wednesday, head down to watch players fight it out to the sounds of traditional music.

The players slide along the cobblestones while attempting to score by hitting the ball into the post using just their hips. 

There’s no Pok Ta Pok league (the game is re-created for entertainment purposes) but that doesn’t mean that it isn’t a fun and exciting spectacle that you can catch every week while living in Merida.

### 9\. Grab a Drink (or Two, or Three)

Happy hour runs late in Merida, and there’s no shortage of places to grab cervezas, margaritas, micheladas, or palomas. You can even try pox (pronounced poche) which is a regional specialty drink made from corn.

If traditional cantinas aren’t your thing, there’s a growing craft beer scene with new options popping up in the centro all the time.

### 10\. Dance in the Streets During a Weekly Fiesta

There’s something to do every night in Merida! At night the city’s streets and plazas light up and come to life with dances, performances, concerts, and more. 

On weekends, several of the main streets are closed to traffic and street performers spill out into the streets. 

Featuring regional music and dance, these events are open to the public and are often lined with food trucks and pop-up stalls in case you feel hungry after dancing the night away.

### Living in Merida Mexico

Now that you’ve learned about all there is to see and do in Merida, it’s time to find your dream property! [Contact us today](https://www.meridarealestategroup.com/contact-us/)
 to enjoy luxury, upscale living in Merida, Mexico.
